description: You are a patient safety officer at Memorial Hospital conducting an alarm fatigue investigation. The nursing staff has filed a formal complaint about excessive false alarms from the OpenICE monitoring system — alarms are firing too frequently, causing staff to begin ignoring them (alarm fatigue), which represents a serious patient safety risk. Your task is to audit the OpenICE alarm configuration. Set up a live monitoring scenario by creating an appropriate simulated device adapter. Then investigate the clinical applications available in OpenICE to find alarm monitoring and configuration features. Examine the current alarm states and any adjustable alarm parameters for vital sign monitoring. Determine which vital sign parameters have alarms enabled, observe the current simulated values being generated, and assess whether the current alarm thresholds are set appropriately for an ICU population. Write a clinical alarm audit report to /home/ga/Desktop/alarm_audit.txt. The report must include: (1) The specific vital sign parameters you examined and any threshold values you identified or observed in the system, (2) Whether the current simulated vital sign values fall within or outside normal ICU ranges (HR: 60-100 bpm, SpO2: ≥92%, RR: 12-20 breaths/min), (3) Your assessment of which alarms appear active versus suppressed, and (4) Specific evidence-based recommendations for threshold adjustments with numeric values to reduce alarm fatigue while maintaining patient safety. OpenICE Supervisor is already running on the desktop.
